query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a uniformly dispersed, ductile, low‐melting metallic phase into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy will enhance its mechanical integrity by impeding crack initiation and propagation while preserving its large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy exhibiting high caloric performance but poor mechanical integrity and a tendency to crack.
generation.intervention: Incorporate a rare-earth–free, low‐melting, ductile metallic phase (e.g., an In-based alloy) into the high-entropy alloy to create a composite structure with improved load transfer.
generation.conditions: Under operational applied magnetic and pressure fields and within the temperature range where the caloric effect is active, subjected to typical compressive loading regimes.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of coherent or semi-coherent interfaces between the ductile secondary phase and the high-entropy alloy matrix mediates improved load transfer and crack inhibition.
generation.mechanism: The ductile phase absorbs energy during mechanical loading, reducing stress concentrations near microstructural flaws and thus delaying crack propagation, while its limited volume fraction minimizes interference with the caloric phase transition.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in compressive strength by roughly 30–50% compared to the unmodified alloy, with key caloric response parameters (transition temperature, latent heat, entropy change) maintained within approximately 10% of baseline values.
generation.baseline: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy shows excellent caloric performance but is brittle with a tendency to crack under load.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is expected to hold under moderate field strengths and temperature ranges that activate the caloric response. Extreme conditions, such as very high temperatures or loading regimes that could trigger excessive softening or phase separation of the ductile phase, fall outside the anticipated operational window.
generation.uncertainty: Some uncertainty remains regarding the precise volume fraction of the ductile phase required to optimize both mechanical integrity and caloric performance.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare composite samples of the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy with 5–10 vol.% of a low-melting, rare-earth–free ductile metallic phase (e.g., an In-based alloy) uniformly distributed. Perform compressive strength tests and measure the caloric response (transition temperature, latent heat, and entropy change) under controlled applied magnetic and pressure fields. Characterize the microstructure using electron microscopy to confirm phase dispersion and interface quality, and compare the results to those of pure alloy samples.
measurements: Caloric performance metrics (transition temperature, latent heat, entropy change)
Microstructural analysis (phase dispersion and interface coherence)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the composite samples show less than a 10% degradation in caloric performance or less than approximately a 30% increase in compressive strength compared to the unmodified alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: Incorporating a uniformly dispersed, ductile, rare‐earth–free low‐melting metallic phase (such as an In-based alloy) into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy will enhance its compressive strength and integrity by impeding crack initiation and propagation, while preserving its large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
drafts.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy exhibiting excellent caloric performance but poor mechanical integrity and tendency to crack.
drafts.intervention: Introduce a secondary phase by in situ forming or incorporating a ductile, low-melting metallic phase (e.g., an In-based alloy) into the high-entropy alloy to create a composite structure.
drafts.conditions: Under applied magnetic and pressure fields at operational temperatures where the caloric effect is active and under typical compressive loading regimes; the intervention should be evaluated under moderate field strengths and temperature ranges that do not activate unwanted phase transformations.
drafts.structural_mediator: The formation of coherent or semi-coherent interfaces between the ductile secondary phase and the high-entropy alloy matrix will mediate improved load transfer and inhibit crack propagation.
drafts.mechanism: The ductile phase acts as an energy absorber during mechanical loading, reducing stress concentrations at flaws and preventing premature failure. At the same time, careful control of its volume fraction and interface characteristics minimizes interference with the intrinsic caloric transition of the matrix.
drafts.predicted_outcome: An increase in compressive strength by approximately 30–50% compared to the unmodified alloy, with caloric response parameters (transition temperature, latent heat, and entropy change) maintained within a 10% variation relative to the baseline performance.
drafts.baseline: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits high caloric performance but suffers from brittle behavior and cracking under stress.
drafts.boundary: The effectiveness of the intervention is expected to hold under moderate magnetic and pressure fields and within the temperature range where the alloy’s caloric effect is operative. Extreme temperatures or loading conditions that might cause excessive softening or phase separation of the reinforcer are outside the expected operational envelope.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare composite samples containing 5–10 vol.% of a low-melting, rare-earth–free ductile metallic phase (e.g., an In-based alloy) uniformly distributed in the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy. Conduct compressive strength tests and measure caloric response (transition temperature, latent heat, and entropy change) under controlled applied magnetic and pressure fields. Characterize the microstructure using electron microscopy to confirm phase dispersion and interface quality. Compare these results with control samples of the pure alloy.
measurements: Caloric performance metrics (transition temperature, latent heat, entropy change)
Microstructural analysis (phase dispersion and interface coherence)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the composite samples exhibit less than a 10% increase in compressive strength compared to the unmodified alloy, or if the caloric response deteriorates by more than 10% (in any key metric), the hypothesis is falsified.
